## Natural history notes

A large wood-boring moth characterized by mottled gray-brown forewings, a heavy body, and bark-like patterning that helps adults blend into tree trunks. In Florida, it is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, parks, yards, orchards, and other wooded areas where suitable host trees occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars tunnel into the trunks and branches of hardwood trees such as oak, maple, ash, willow, and fruit trees, creating galleries in the wood and serving as prey for woodpeckers and other insect-eating animals.
